I'm a distance runner that lives in the upper midwest. I prefer to run outside, but the winter time always made for difficulties.

Up to 3 years ago, I would sign up at a gym around November/December and keep the membership through March/April, just so I could use their treadmills. Most have an indoor track, but the lanes were always clogged with walkers. This often involved a non-refundable set up fee or a termination fee. It sucked, but that was the price for indoor running. It was cheaper than buying a decent treadmill.

The thing is, I absolutely hate treadmills. I call them "dreadmills."

3 years ago, when the winter of 2014-2015 crept upon us, and my outdoor route was turning icy, instead of going to the gym, I bought spikes for my shoes, and invested in cold weather gear (thank you cheap "C9 by Champion" gear at Target). That winter, despite the snow, blowing blizzard winds, compacted ice and snow on the roads, and temperatures in the -20F to -10F range (before wind chill), I got my ass outside and ran 10Ks (or more) every other day.
